summary: Tubten Chokyi Dorje studied under Jamgön Kongtröl Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He taught Dilgo Khyentse, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Khenpo Shenga.
Tubten Gyeltsen Ozer studied under Jamgön Kongtröl Lodrö Thaye, Patrul Rinpoche, and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo.

A scholar in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, Tubten Nyendrak (1883–1959) studied under Jamgön Kongtröl Lodrö Thaye, Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso, and Khenpo Shenga. He taught Botrul Dongak Tenpai Nyima and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.
Tubten Nyima was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, and taught Steven Neal Weinberger.
Tubten Tsondru studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Dodrupchen Rinpoche, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Khenpo Gangshar. He taught Khenchen Palden Sherab Rinpoche and Ringu Tulku.
Specializing in Indology and linguistics, Tukaram Ramchandra Laddu studied at the University of Halle until 1912. He held a post at Sampurnanand Sanskrit University, attested in 1920.
Tulku Hungkar Dorje studied under Penor Rinpoche and Dodrupchen Rinpoche.

Born in 1961, Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar Tulku Sherdor studied at Vassar College, Naropa University, and the University of Virginia. He studied under Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Ted Norton, and Jeffrey Hopkins.

Tulku Thondup (1939–2023) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied at Dodrupchen Monastery and under Kyala Khenpo, Khenpo Chemchok, and Dodrupchen Rinpoche, later serving as a visiting scholar at Harvard University.

Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche (1920–1996) was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar who founded Tergar Osel Ling Monastery. He studied under Samten Gyatso, Dilgo Khyentse, Jamyang Khyentse Chökyi Lodrö, Karsé Kongtrul, and Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, teaching numerous students.

Turrell V. Wylie (1927–1984) worked in Tibetology, Sinology, and linguistics. He earned his B.A. from the University of Washington, studying with Giuseppe Tucci and Dezhung Rinpoche, and became Associate Professor (1959) and Professor (1970) at Washington.
Tutob Chökyi Wangchuk studied under Dilgo Khyentse, Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, and Trulshik Rinpoche.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Tyler Dewar studied at Nitartha Institute (attested 2008, 2019). He also studied under Acharya Tashi Wangchuk from 2003 to 2004 and under Dzogchen Ponlop Rinpoche (attested 2019).

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tzungkuen Wen completed his PhD at the University of Queensland in 2009 under Primož Pecenko, Tamara Ditrich, and Chris Kang. He also studied under Yangzhu Xu, Nandasiri Sayadaw, and Sayadaw U Pandita, lecturing at Fuyan Buddhist Institute in 2005.

Tōru Funayama (born 1961) is a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Sinology who studied at Kyoto University and under Ernst Steinkellner. He was Associate Professor at Kyushu University (1999–2003) and Professor at Kyoto University (attested 1995–2019).

U Ba Khin (1899–1971) worked in Buddhist and religious studies and founded the International Meditation Centre. He studied under Saya Thetgyi (Saya Thet Gyi) between approximately 1937 and 1945, and taught Mother Sayamagyi and Satya Narayan Goenka.

Sayadaw U Pandita (1921–2016) worked in Buddhist and religious studies, studying under Nandasiri Sayadaw and Mahasi Sayadaw. He taught at Mahasi Sasana Yeiktha from 1955, succeeded Mahasi Sayadaw (1982–1991), and founded and served as abbot of Panditarama Meditation Center.
Active in Tibetology and history/archaeology, Ugyen Pelgen earned a Master's degree from Aligarh Muslim University and served as a lecturer of History at Sherubtse College.

Specializing in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, Ulrich Pagel studied under Tadeusz Skorupski, Philip Denwood, and Renate Söhnen-Thieme. He held a post at SOAS University of London (attested 2013–2020).

Ulrich Timme Kragh (born 1969) studied at Karmapa International Buddhist Institute and the University of Copenhagen. A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and Indology, he held positions at Copenhagen, Harvard, Geumgang University, IIAS, the University of Sydney, and ANU.
